events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Challenge

options.text: If that is what you want, I will end you by my own hand.
You are a fool, [character]. Guards!

events.text: [character] face is grim. "I didn't want it to come to this, [character]. But we both know all is not as it should be in [rival]. If no one else here is brave enough to say it, I will: You have grown complacent, old, and most of all, weak." He holds his blade aloft and booms, "Face my sword, blade to blade. Show me I'm wrong. Or just rot there on that throne, and let [rival] rot with you."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Gruesome Example

options.text: This is no time to show weakness.
I will never condone such barbarity.

events.text: [character] worries that our enemies do not truly fear our armies. He wishes to order that in all future conflicts, prisoners will not be taken. Generals and other officers will be executed and raised on stakes above the battlefield. Such a directive may intimidate our enemies, but at what cost?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Knife at Your Side

options.text: A masterstroke [character] will never suspect.
The risks are too great...

events.text: [character] has been slowly developing a network of contacts and conspirators, with the ultimate goal of removing that thorn in the side of your reign, [character]. Late one night over drinks, [character] shares his plans. How do you react?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Lit Match

options.text: So be it, I will have [character] by my side.
This is getting out of hand. We need not further fan the flames of [character] pride.

events.text: [character] renown and determination has only continued to grow. By now, [rival] is running out of accolades to ceremonially bestow. There are now public calls that he should be elevated to the royal family by marriage, and even some of your closest advisors agree it could be safer to have him in the inner circle than outside of it.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A New Method

options.text: Apply it to a project currently in development.
Provide our scientists with better practices.
Create a process that enhances efficiency.

events.text: In his time away from court, [character] has been investing in a variety of scientific pursuits. He comes to you with an exciting new development: a method with which scholars may gain knowledge by observation and deduction. [character] believes this discovery will revolutionize scientific pursuits, but he is not sure how best to use it.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Promotion

options.text: Overseer of the Fields.
Possessor of Veneration.
Steward of the Chamber.

events.text: Your Courtier, [character], approaches the court about a title change. He feels overlooked in the court and believes his energy and expertise could be used more productively. What shall we name him?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Scholar Denounced

options.text: [character]’s ideas are far too dangerous.
That is not for [character] to decide.
Explain that the findings actually compliment [religion].

events.text: "I am concerned," a well-dressed reads out a message from [character], "by the recent findings of the godless scholar [character] at your court. Unchecked, these ideas could pose a threat to the spread of [religion]. Denounce his work and the rest of the court should follow." The is watching expectantly. How do you respond?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Superior System

options.text: Release our people from servitude.
The current laws are working as intended.
We will work harder to care for our people.

events.text: Your trusted advisor, [character], recently visited the [rival] court on a diplomatic mission, and he liked what he saw. "The [rival] conquer foreign lands for labor. It is a far superior system." [character] proposes we change the current laws. "Why break the backs of our people, when we can make others shoulder the burden?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A United Front

options.text: Accept the changes to succession laws.

events.text: [character] has never been an especially popular figure at court... but that has changed as [character] has become something of a personal advocate. Now [character] has an entire faction in [city] clamoring for changes to dynastic succession that would solidify his claims on the throne and bringbring him that much closer to the throne and [character] that much closer to his own ambitions.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Visit From [character]

options.text: You have my attention, [character].
Despite all your supporters, the only things you bring to the table are duplicity, and your own set of enemies.

events.text: You never quite knew where you stood with [character]. You still don't. But now, he claims he wants nothing more than to work together to solidify your rule.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waste of Talent

options.text: [character] shall serve as a Grand Vizier.
Let them clamor. [character] cannot be trusted.

events.text: Voices in the court are clamoring for more [character]. They say he has been languishing on the sidelines, when he should be putting his talents to work for [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Waste of Talent

options.text: [character] shall serve as a Grand Vizier.
Let them clamor. [character] cannot be trusted.

events.text: Voices in the court are clamoring for more [character]. They say he has been languishing on the sidelines, when he should be putting his talents to work for [rival].

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: A Wild Night

options.text: I can resist anything, except temptation!

events.text: The party is in full swing, the orgy is reaching its climax, and the wine fountain has run dry and been refilled twice already. You are contemplating calling for when [character] approaches you,. “I say, [character],” he exclaims, “this is the best party I’ve been to in years! Thank you ever so much!” You grin in reply, “Think nothing of it!” and return to your contemplation. Before you can reach any conclusion you are distracted by the sight of [character]. Since he looks to be having so much fun, you decide to join him.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Audited

options.text: Pay off all financial inconsistencies at once.
Make [character] a merchant of the court.

events.text: One morning, [character] arrives in court with a group of scribes and scholars bearing armfuls of scrolls. According to his long-winded oratory, he has finished an extensive audit of royal financial records. The findings reveal a history of inefficient practices and embezzled funds. [character] demands that you address these concerns immediately.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Breaking the Fear

options.text: Imprison someone as an example. [character] shall know true terror.
I shall favor another member of the court instead.
We shall reconcile our differences.

events.text: Reports have arrived concerning [character]. It seems he is no longer terrified of you. How shall we handle this matter?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Closing the Deal

options.text: Research from their distinguished scientists.
Assistance with court and legal matters.
Infrastructure for our military forces.
A promise for the future.

events.text: Working his numerous trade connections, [character] has informally negotiated a generous arrangement with [rival]. For some of [character]'s wise counsel, the [rival] are willing to offer us a variety of tributes. He leaves the decision up to the court.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Community Chest

options.text: Let them contribute food.
Let them contribute stone.
Let them contribute wood.
I need no recognition.

events.text: Impressed by your thoughtful and reserved presence atop the throne, elders from [city] have come to offer a blessing. They wish to raise you up as an example to all the leaders across [rival]. As part of this ritual blessing, they will collect gifts from the community.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Divinity Calls

options.text: [character], and this enthusiasm, could be easily co-opted by throwing state support behind their beliefs.
[character] can carry on with his own endeavors. It is not our concern.

events.text: [character] has developed an unmatched popularity across [rival], but for the [religion], he is seen as both savior and champion.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Divinity Calls

options.text: [character], and this enthusiasm, could be easily co-opted by throwing state support behind their beliefs.
[character] can carry on with his own endeavors. It is not our concern.

events.text: [character] has developed an unmatched popularity across [rival], but for the [religion], he is seen as both savior and champion.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Economic Juggernaut

options.text: Grant [character] powers of economic oversight.
Keep [character] on the sidelines.

events.text: [character] has accomplished the near impossible - creating a wave of discussion and excitement through the court about fiscal theory. His ideas on Monetary Reform have captured the popular imagination, and calls for [character] to be given the powers needed to implement those ideas are growing.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: False Outlook

options.text: Something about this strikes me as false.
We need all the help we can get.
Perhaps we should enlist foreign-born troops.

events.text: Ongoing conflicts stretch our resources thin, and the will of the people weakens with every passing day. [character] comes to the court with an idea to boost public opinion. He suggests altering news so that it presents a positive outlook. Proclaim losses as victories, tragedies as successes. Scribes and scholars across [rival] would support this narrative, generating the needed support to help us regain our footing in the wars.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Faultless

options.text: I would be honored to call [character] son.
Utter foolishness, to even consider such a thing.

events.text: Since rising to public attention, [character] has proven again and again an asset to [rival], pairing clever insight with unwavering loyalty. Now, without a child of your own to take the reins of [rival], the question circulates through court of whether perhaps [character] should be officially adopted into the royal line.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Favored [family] Son

options.text: I shall not fight my own countrymen. Invite [character] to the [city] palace to discuss a peaceful transition.
I want [character] seized and every [family] holding surrounded. If they think I shall waver, they are sorely mistaken.

events.text: The ultimatum will arrive any day, you have been assured. [character] is no longer an untested young man of promise, but a juggernaut of [rival], and the pride and hope of house [family]. If [character] is ready to claim the throne, they will back him with everything they can muster.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Founding Signs

options.text: Our scouts will search for suitable sites.
This is not the time for expansion.

events.text: After days of meditation, royal seers suggest that this would be an auspicious time to found a new city. They have seen a glorious future. Shall the court consider it?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Fruits of the Noble Path

options.text: [character] should follow this life of piety.
How inspiring!

events.text: [character] is no longer one of the unenlightened common people. Instead, he has set out on the long path to enlightenment through studying the [religion] dharma and following the teachings of the Buddha. To abandon his earthly fetters will take a lifetime, if he succeeds at all.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Goodbye to All That

options.text: Erect a monument in his name.
He never understood my vision.

events.text: One of our most veteran generals, [character], has grown weary of our endless wars. He is retiring to a rural villa to enjoy the rest of his days as a man of peace and solitude. Shall we consider a tribute?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Inward Gaze

options.text: [character] speaks the truth, and we must change.
[rival] needs help from no one.
Remind [character] to have pride in his nation.

events.text: "I cannot stay silent any longer," your son [character] says before the court. "Our inward gaze diminishes our influence in the world. It makes us small, ignorant, and feeble." He advocates fiercely for new laws promoting exploration, diplomacy, and trade. Advisors and diplomats burst into applause, showing a rare enthusiasm.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Knowledge is Power

options.text: Inform [character] of what you know, and of his obligations.
Inform the court of what you know.

events.text: [character] is slowly becoming a serious problem. He has been seen approaching various notables of [rival], gauging their loyalties and obligations. It seems only a matter of time before he makes some sort of move, no doubt to your detriment. Fortunately, you know a great deal more about [character] than you suspect he is aware. Secret affairs with married <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_STRAIGHT_MAN>women<p=SUBJECT_STRAIGHT_WOMAN>men<p=SUBJECT_NOT_STRAIGHT_MAN>men<p=SUBJECT_NOT_STRAIGHT_WOMAN>women<else>lovers<end>, acts of cowardice, sacrilege, lies - it is quite the portfolio.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Legends of Mithra

options.text: Mithra will lead our warriors to battle.
He must be watching over my agreements.

events.text: The sunrise takes your breath away, climbing over the roofs of [city] with a glorious blood red glow. Your mind wanders to the teachings of [religion], which tell of how Mithra battles the powers of darkness every morning so that the sun may rise, driving across the sky in his chariot drawn by four white steeds. Others argue that the sun is the eye of Mithra, rising above the earth so that he may watch over the deals made by mankind. Perhaps this wonder is a sign from the guardian god himself?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Master of Poisons

options.text: Intrigue must remain "honorable."
Poisons are a powerful shadow weapon.

events.text: Our spymaster approaches us with an unusual request: a laboratory for poisons. As he explains it, additional research into poisons and venomous creatures would increase his ability to combat intrigue. "Daggers can be so... messy," he explains.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Meddling from [city]

options.text: Let [character] have his victory, and the [family] their petty local laws.
[city] rules, and the rest of [rival] follows. On this I will not bend.

events.text: Of late, the [family] have complained louder and louder about overreach and inefficient management from the capital. And [character], well, his voice has been the loudest and most persuasive of them all.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Might of Nations

options.text: We need all the soldiers we can find.
Recruit only the purest [rival] for our ranks.

events.text: During his many travels and campaigns, [character] has witnessed firsthand the might of other tribes and nations. Now he has requested that we expand our military recruitment to include foreign citizens living in [rival]. Of course, [character] wants nothing to do with those born outside our borders, believing them at best to be slobs and cowards, at worst spies. He grates at [character]'s suggestion.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Mouthpiece of the Gods

options.text: My words must outlive me.
We cannot afford such a project.

events.text: Your proclamations have inspired the kingdom, and the people have come to call you "mouthpiece of the gods" for your gifted rhetoric. Perhaps it is time to record your tenets for posterity. Our advisors suggest that we inscribe your precepts on clay cylinders to be erected in every city.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Navy or Army

options.text: Ships are a great assets - we need more of them!
The problem with ships is how costly they are. We should be able to find more resources for our military buildup somewhere!

tip: As leader: Effect Unit Trait: Ship → Naval Detractor Ship
As leader: Effect Unit Trait: Infantry → Naval Detractor Infantry

options.text: It is true that ships will never deal [rival] a crushing blow. We will gradually dismantle our navy and improve the ground forces!

events.text: Our ongoing war against [rival] raises the question of our navy's importance at the court. [rival] possesses ships that can be a great asset in war, but they are also expensive and slow to build. Detractors of the navy argue that no ship can ever capture a city or defeat the [rival] army directly. We should therefore, they claim, focus on the army. Supporters of naval investment are quick to point out that nothing compares to the mobility of ships and that we will find it much easier to fight [rival] soldiers if our navy lets us choose the time and place of any battle as well as intercept [rival] supply. What do you think about the future of the [rival] military?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Obligations

options.text: What a fine mess [character] has made. I shall gladly wash my hands of it.

events.text: [character] has promised great things for [rival], and for a great many people, and received much in return. There's just one catch. These promises have thus far remained mostly unfulfilled, and, [character] admits, it might be that some among the interested parties have - somehow - been under the misapprehension that you have guaranteed these commitments.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Of the People

options.text: May my modesty serve as an example.
Yes, a ruler must embrace the role.

events.text: Your ascetic lifestyle makes you popular among the people of [city]. They praise your thrift in the streets and markets of the city! But while your frugality may appeal to the average citizen, noble Family are beginning to grumble. The [family] have called for you to behave in a way more befitting your station.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Parental Guidance

options.text: To lead is to be in front of your people, not above them.
You can only be stabbed in the back if you let someone get too close.
Save money and it will multiply tenfold. Spend freely, and you will soon be spending tenfold.

events.text: A letter arrives from your heir, [character]. It reads: "Father, I am proud beyond words to serve the people of [city] as their governor. Managing a city's affairs is no easy task, yet I will take the throne one day, and every night I pray for wisdom to be worthy to call myself your son. As I seek my own path, would you honor me with advice on how to be the best ruler I can be?"

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Personal Enrichment

options.text: Sometimes, prices must be paid.
Do you think me blind, [character], or merely impotent?

events.text: Grand Vizier is a powerful position. [character] has learned well how to wield that power, primarily for his own benefit. Whatever happens in [rival], [character] gets a cut, and so, in turn, does every functionary and officer follow his example.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Pleasure Banquet

options.text: No, it is time to retire for the night.
Bring on the songs! Bring on the lively debate!
This is a good time for drunken diplomacy.

events.text: The day begins humbly enough... but athletic contests lead to poetic readings, and a musical concert evolves into a rousing dramatic performance. By the end of the evening, revelers have taken to the couches, and servants work to replenish the banquet table. Two men enter the banquet hall carrying another jar of wine between them. The celebration has only just begun!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Political Influence

options.text: Start a whisper campaign to rally the [family].
Give the [family] an ultimatum: join us, or suffer.

events.text: [character], our political ally, grows concerned that the [family] family's unhappiness may widen rifts in the court. He volunteers to meet with key individuals in the [family] household, which will hopefully bring them into alignment with our efforts. "There are other methods," he murmurs. "I know some ruffians in need of work. Nothing wins allies like a good threat."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Preemptive Strike

options.text: He is correct. Now is the time.
The [tribe] have done nothing to us.
Build up our forces in case of an attack.

events.text: Once again, [character] brings his concern about the [tribe] to the court's attention. Only this time he demands action. Convinced that the [tribe] are building their armies in preparation for an attack, [character] wishes to launch a pre-emptive strike. How shall we respond?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Pressing the Point

options.text: Thrust the sword.
Drop the sword.
Call for guards.

events.text: It is only a ceremonial sword in your hand, but it's sharp enough. [character] presses his neck to the blade. "If you truly believe that I am wrong, strike me down now. If you truly think you have the courage to hold the [rival] throne, show it." His voice raises. "Let all bear witness! If [character] possesses neither the courage of his own conviction, nor the wisdom to stand aside, why should you allow his reign?"

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Raja-rishi

options.text: I will do all in my power to aid them.
The loyalty of the people is the greatest reward I could ask for.
I must strive to be better, to live up to their expectations.

events.text: Known for your discipline and self-control, the people have been praising you as Raja-rishi, the Sage King. They are aware that the greatest enemies of the [title] are his own flaws, the lapses of character that can lead a nation to ruin. You have shown the determination to be better. People follow you not for your title, but for your character; the greatest of compliments.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Rare Talent

options.text: Patience is the key.

events.text: Having taken up games of chance socially, you have unearthed a substantial talent for making consistent winnings.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Reforms Program

options.text: I trust your assessment, [character].
I cannot allow you to upend systems and laws that have served [rival] for generations.

events.text: [character] is determined. [rival] can run better, he assures you. "Yes, it will take time. Yes, there will be costs. Yes, there will be resistance, but I promise you, [rival] will be the stronger for it."

events.author: Andy Auseon

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

events.name: Religious Law

options.text: The court shall adopt these measures.
It is not right to mix law and religion.

events.text: [character] of the [family] family makes a speech to the court, encouraging us to align our laws with the teachings of [religion]. He believes that obeying a strict code of social norms is the only way to achieve the blessings of the divine. Many in the court find wisdom in his words.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Rope and Winch

options.text: We will never condone such barbaric acts.
Cruelty is the only way to reach the truth.
Perhaps [character] would let me watch.

events.text: The great soldier [character] has shown a peculiar interest in the recently developed windlass apparatus. He believes that its rope-and-winch mechanism could be utilized for somewhat "untraditional" means, namely torture. [character] has requested that we allow him to experiment on prisoners from the dungeons.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Science or Magic?

options.text: [character] stays, but he will be watched.
Such behavior is either madness or treason.

events.text: Stories about the strange powers of the scientist [character] have reached the court. According to rumors, he has been seen in several locations at once, can speak to creatures in their natural tongues, and is known to make astounding predictions. There is a rumbling of dissent among his followers. If [character] is seen as a "divine" figure, what is to keep him from the throne?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Silent War

options.text: Set [character] to testing the officials in [city] to ensure none have been turned.
Send agents to create chaos in the [rival] ranks.
Send a poison-girl to [character].

events.text: Open war is not the only route to victory, [character] explains. When the chaos of war is a risk not worth taking, there are other ways to undermine and weaken the enemy. [character] agents suspect that [rival] is preparing for war with [rival], and the Spymaster suggests that direct, yet covert, action be taken.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Taboos

options.text: Never, the human body is sacred.
We must know all we can about ourselves.
[character] will supply him with the... "subjects" required.

events.text: A frustrated [character] appears before the court. He explains that [rival] cultural taboos against human dissection are limiting medical research. If using remains for scientific research was not so condemned, the nation could make great leaps forward. Many frown upon such procedures, but the decision falls to you.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Tax Hike

options.text: Everyone should expect to make sacrifices.
A leader must spare the people from pain.

events.text: Your Merchant [character] proposes a new policy to increase the kingdom's production. "However, it may affect your reputation... negatively." A one-off tax will anger the people, but the benefit in Money may be worth it.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Tedium on the Throne

tip: As leader: +50 Unit Trait XP / Mounted
As governor: +100 Unit Trait XP / Mounted

options.text: Appoint my horse to the ruling council.
Attend every event garbed as a god.
I need to make some changes in my life.

events.text: Managing the affairs of the kingdom has grown tedious. You would prefer to spend more time indulging in the various privileges that come with power and position. There must be something more interesting than taxes, levies, and laws. How will you enjoy your status as ruler of this earthly domain?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The City to Come

options.text: Let [character] raise the first stones!

events.text: [character] has been drawing up plans, gathering resources, surveying sites, and at last he is satisfied with a new plan of development to make [city] the shining jewel he has always envisioned.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Curse of Knowledge

options.text: We shall begin speaking in the popular manner.
I better lay off the philosophy tomes.
Wisdom is all! We dare not let these uncouth fools hold us back.

events.text: While you are speaking with your courtiers about matters most monumental and revelatory, you notice that they don't fully understand the luminosity of your diatribes. How shall we remedy this?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Mahabharata

options.text: Such horror should be avoided at all costs.
With checks and balances, perhaps.
We do what we must.

events.text: The Great Tale tells of generations of kings and empires locked in a war of succession. Interleaved between the dramatic twists of fate and heroism are explorations of what it means to live righteously and definitions of a just way of life. With the war against [rival] forefront in your mind, one passage in particular holds your attention: One of the princes asks, can the suffering of war ever be justified?

events.author: Andy Auseon
conditions: Not Any Descendant Of Leader Us
events.name: The Map and the Dagger

options.text: Attempt to evade his blows.
Rely on your loyal guards.

events.text: [character] invites you to [city] for a guided tour of some of the improvements and expansions he has planned for the city. You stop on a cliffside overlooking the breadth of [city]. Unrolling his proposed plans, [character] reveals a dagger hidden within the map's rolls. He prepares to strike a killing blow.

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: The Pagan Colleges

options.text: We would be able to cover these expense, but with a few requirements.
Sorry, we can't afford to lose your services to the court.

events.text: You are approached by [character] who looks more pensive than usual with heavy bags under her eyes. She explains that she wishes to leave the court to work on the organization of colleges for [religion] now that [rival] has embraced Polytheism. There is also a small wrinkle, a lack of funding, which she hopes you can remedy. We would lose a valuable courtier and pay a hefty sum, but perhaps the long term benefits would outweigh the costs?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Song of God

options.text: Through meditation.
Through insight and reflection.
Through righteous action.
Through love and devotion.

events.text: One passage from the Mahabharata, the Bhagavad Gita, has gained particular popularity and prominence across all of the schools of [religion]. The dialogue between the prince Arjuna and his charioteer, the god Kishna, has endless interpretations as to the relation between the individual and the divine. In one particularly popular part, it describes four paths to self-realization. Which route sings to you?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Time Has Come

options.text: You think you have all the answers? Then you are a fool, but I suppose better a fool on the throne than a divided [rival].
You have courage, I'll grant you that. I will give you ten days to be gone from [rival] for good. Be grateful for my mercy.
It is nothing personal, but I will enjoy seeing your death.

events.text: [character] looks you square in the eyes. "It is nothing personal, [character], but I have seen the state of [rival]. I know what it needs to flourish, and it is not your rulership. I cannot stand by and watch my beloved nation continue on its current course - if you step down you will be hailed as a wise and humble king, or you can continue on and risk ruin."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Universal Order

options.text: Provide him with whatever is needed.
We cannot afford these explorations.
Copy and distribute this important work.

events.text: After months of toil, great scientist [character] has finished a treatise on the natural world. This tome, titled "The Universal Order of [character]," proposes a strict classification system for all living things. [character] seeks additional support to continue research.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Upper Hand

options.text: Use the information to rein in [character].
[character] time in [rival] is at an end.

requirements.label: Terrifying
tip: The leader must have Terrifying (a character trait)

options.text: There will be no mercy or negotiation with treason.

events.text: Secret meetings between [rival] and [character]? It can hardly be believed, and yet your sources have confirmed it beyond a doubt.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Wild Hunters

options.text: Go forth, my hunters!
No, such titles will distract from their training.

events.text: Your [unit] are already skilled, but [character] has an offer to push their abilities even further. A talented pathfinder, [character] has offered to show a select unit the hidden routes and tracks that cover [rival], training them in the art of the hunt so they may chase down any that dare enter our territory.

events.author: Josh Unsworth

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

events.name: To Take the Cloth

fields: AddTraitReligion: RELIGION_ZOROASTRIANISM, RELIGION_JUDAISM, RELIGION_CHRISTIANITY, RELIGION_MANICHAEISM, RELIGION_PAGAN_AKSUM, RELIGION_PAGAN_ASSYRIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_BABYLONIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_CARTHAGE, RELIGION_PAGAN_EGYPT, RELIGION_PAGAN_GREECE, RELIGION_PAGAN_KUSH, RELIGION_PAGAN_ROME, RELIGION_PAGAN_PERSIA, RELIGION_PAGAN_HITTITE, RELIGION_ATENISM, RELIGION_HINDUISM, RELIGION_BUDDHISM

options.text: Yes, [character] would be an asset to [religion].
No, he is best suited elsewhere.

events.text: [character] has recently taken [character] under his wing, teaching the eager pupil the rituals and rites that make up the [religion] faith. [character] reports that [character] is an exceptional learner and requests further time together in order to train him as. While remaining at your court as a courtier, the new would also answer to [character]. Should [character] be allowed to join the clergy?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Trusted

options.text: Organize an auxiliary force.
Send the volunteers back to [city] for training.

events.text: Your time on the frontiers has earned you a reputation as a general of skill and a defender of the people. Everywhere you pass, young people are eager to sign on to your banner, determined to be part of something magnificent. What is to be done with all these eager new recruits?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Unethical Practices

options.text: This is all part of a working economy.
The warning should be backed up with economic reforms.
Send your soldiers to crack some skulls.

events.text: Court merchant [character] has voiced concerns about the habits of traders in the city markets. Apparently, rampant acts of usury are bringing many families to the brink of ruin. [character] wishes to quash further unfair lending, and he looks to us for guidance.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Unflinching

options.text: I did not want to see it, but once spoken, it is clear.
I think I know a jackal when I see one.

events.text: [character] eyes are like iron and do not waver as he speaks. "I do not say this lightly, but do not allow [character] to follow you on the throne." "It is only truth, not cruelty, to say he has the morals of a jackal and the attention span of a child. Do not allow him to make [rival] his personal playground."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wall of Battle

options.text: We will release [character] from his obligations.
He still has so much to give to the court in his current duties.
I will contribute to his great work of art.

events.text: [character] has always been a dreamer, a philosopher, a student of the arts and sciences. As he advances in age, he considers how to use the years he has left. Inspired by the heroics of our [rival] armies, [character] decides to leave the court to pursue a lifelong goal: a glorious public mural depicting the great battles of our age. Of course, he would like you to bless this endeavor.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wisdom Literature

options.text: His lessons should be heeded by all.
Scribes are too valuable to waste.

events.text: A royal tutor, [character] wishes to record his teachings for posterity. They would take the form of relatable stories meant to impart valuable lessons. He calls this project "wisdom literature." Is this wise use of our scribes, or should [character] be focused on other matters?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wisdom with Age

options.text: Transition to seniority rule.
Keep the current succession.

events.text: As you grow older, you begin to recognize the advantages of age and experience. You have brought a lifetime of wisdom to bear on the destiny of this nation. Our ministers believe your reign makes a strong case for changing the law so that the right of succession belongs to the oldest living relative. Of course, such a shift may offend the current heir, [character].

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Wood Shortages

options.text: Request wood shipments from [rival].
Build emergency lumbermills in [city].
Recruit more village woodcutters.
Do nothing for now.

events.text: Court soldier [character] has spent the last several months reviewing our military, and he concludes that the nation's supply of wood is grossly insufficient. Pikes, spears, arrows, and siege equipment will all require more lumber than the mills and loggers can produce. Is this a problem to face for today, or one we can push off until tomorrow?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Call to Arms

options.text: Such betrayal cannot be forgiven.

events.text: Perhaps at one time you could have found common ground with [character], reached some form of compromise. But that time is done. He has sworn to dethrone you, or die in the attempt.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [character] Reach

options.text: [character] is forcing my hand.
If this is the price of [character] cooperation, so be it.

events.text: [character] died by all accounts swiftly, and without audible final words. [character] has taken no effort to hide his hand in the matter, nor does he make any denials when confronted. "Some things need doing, and someone willing to do them," is all [character] says before his departure preempts even a nod of dismissal.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Due

options.text: Defy [rival].

events.text: They say the wealth of the world flows into [city], and it certainly seems as though [character] has been tasked with sending [rival] share.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: [tribe] Unrest

options.text: Two men, but [character]'s fate rests on their success.
The time is not right for such a mission.

events.text: [character] reports of unrest in the [tribe] camps, and he believes the time is ripe for intervention. "Two good men," he requests "is all I need to turn enemies into friends." It is a plan rife with risk and danger, but the outcome could be an enduring alliance.
